8 Best Customizable Eyewear Brands for 2026: Find Your Perfect Pair

Written by HBR Staff

Written by

HBR Staff

View full bio

Table of Contents

  • Personalized frames, interchangeable styles, and custom fits for every look
  • The 8 Best Customizable Eyewear Brands
  • Buying Guide: How to Choose a Customizable Eyewear Brand
  • Final Thoughts

Personalized frames, interchangeable styles, and custom fits for every look

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 10:25
Instaread

Glasses used to be a once-a-year decision: pick a frame, commit to it, and live with it until your prescription changed. That mindset is fading fast. A growing group of eyewear brands is treating glasses less like a fixed purchase and more like something you can personalize around your style, face, or lifestyle.

“Customizable” can mean different things depending on the brand. Some let you physically swap parts of a frame after purchase, while others focus on interchangeable lenses, personalized fit, or build-your-own configurations. What they have in common is that customization plays a meaningful role in the product experience, whether that means changing the look after purchase, building a frame to your specifications, customizing the fit, or choosing interchangeable lenses.

The 8 Best Customizable Eyewear Brands

We narrowed the list to eight brands where customization is a meaningful part of the product experience, rather than stretching the definition to include every eyewear company with a basic color or lens selector. Here are the brands that stand out for 2026.

1. Pair Eyewear

Pair Eyewear is one of the clearest examples of customizable eyewear, built around a base frame and interchangeable magnetic “Top Frames.” The tops snap on and off in seconds, allowing wearers to change the look of their glasses without buying an entirely new pair. The system works with prescription and non-prescription eyewear and offers a wide range of colors, patterns, graphics, and collaborations.

The appeal is that customization continues after the initial purchase. Instead of committing to one frame style, customers can build a collection of looks around the same base. For anyone who wants the most fashion-focused and flexible interchangeable system, Pair remains one of the strongest options in the category.

Highlights

  • Magnetic Top Frames swap in seconds
  • Hundreds of styles, colors, and patterns
  • Prescription and non-prescription options
  • Collections for adults and kids
Check Availability

2. Zenni Optical

Zenni earns its place on this list through its customizable rimless eyewear collection. Rather than treating the frame as a fixed shape, Zenni lets shoppers build a rimless pair by selecting the frame, customizing the lens shape, choosing temples, and selecting lens tints and prescription options. The brand explicitly positions the collection as a way to “build your own glasses.”

Explore Trendy Dresses
Clothing

This is a different type of customization from Pair’s interchangeable Tops or Switch’s swappable lenses. The personalization happens during the design process rather than through components that are repeatedly changed after purchase. Still, the ability to control the shape and configuration of the final rimless frame makes Zenni a legitimate option for shoppers who want more control over the finished product.

Highlights

  • Build-your-own rimless eyewear
  • Customizable lens shapes
  • Choice of temples and lens tints
  • Prescription and non-prescription options
Check Availability

3. LINDBERG

LINDBERG takes customization in a more sophisticated direction with its modular building system. Rather than simply choosing one frame color, customers can combine different elements of a design, including colors, sizes, temple lengths, nose pads, and other components. The brand says its system offers more than one billion possible configurations.

The result is eyewear that can be highly personalized before it is made, with the customization extending to both aesthetics and fit. That makes LINDBERG particularly compelling for shoppers who want something more individual than an off-the-shelf frame but don’t necessarily need a system designed for daily style changes.

Highlights

  • More than one billion possible configurations
  • Modular building system
  • Customizable size and temple length
  • Multiple nose-pad and fit options
Check Availability

4. Funoogles

Funoogles brings the interchangeable eyewear concept specifically to children. Its system uses a base frame with interchangeable clips and components that allow kids to change the appearance of their glasses. Depending on the model, different pieces can be used to create new looks without replacing the entire frame.

That makes Funoogles more than a brand that simply offers colorful children’s glasses. The customization is physical and repeatable, giving kids an opportunity to participate in choosing how their eyewear looks. It’s a particularly good fit for younger wearers who may be more enthusiastic about wearing glasses when they can change them to match their personality or mood.

Highlights

  • Interchangeable clips and components
  • Multiple looks from one base frame
  • Designed specifically for children
  • Sunglass options available for compatible frames
Check Availability

5. ro•sham•bo eyewear

ro•sham•bo combines customizable eyewear with a strong emphasis on durability. Its Pops line uses magnets integrated into the frame, allowing compatible top pieces and other components to be attached and removed without tools. The result is a system that lets wearers change the appearance or functionality of their glasses while keeping the same base frame.

The distinction matters, however: the interchangeable system is specific to the Pops line rather than a feature across the entire ro•sham•bo collection. For families looking for a customizable option that prioritizes durability and everyday wear, Pops offers a compelling combination of flexibility and resilience.

Highlights

  • Magnetic components in the Pops system
  • Durable, flexible frame construction
  • Interchangeable style and clip-on options
  • Strong focus on children’s eyewear
Check Availability

6. Switch Vision

Switch Vision takes customization in a more functional direction. Instead of changing the appearance of the frame, its magnetic interchangeable lens system allows wearers to swap lenses according to lighting conditions and activities. One frame can therefore serve multiple purposes without requiring several complete pairs of sunglasses.

That makes the concept particularly useful for outdoor athletes and anyone who regularly moves between different environments. Darker lenses can be used in bright sunlight, while other options can be selected for changing or lower-light conditions. Prescription-compatible models are also available on selected frames, making the system useful beyond purely recreational eyewear.

Highlights

  • Magnetic interchangeable lenses
  • Lens options for changing light conditions
  • Designed for active outdoor use
  • RX-compatible options on selected models
Check Availability

7. Fitz Frames

Fitz Frames approaches customization through fit rather than interchangeable components. Using a smartphone-based facial scan, the company creates frames around the wearer’s individual facial measurements instead of relying solely on standard frame dimensions. Customers can also choose from different styles, colors, and lens options.

The result is a different kind of personalized eyewear experience. Fitz isn’t designed for repeatedly changing the appearance of one frame; its strength is creating a frame that is tailored to the person wearing it. For anyone who has struggled with glasses that are too wide, too narrow, or otherwise uncomfortable, custom-fit technology can be a more meaningful form of customization than simply having more colors to choose from.

Highlights

  • Smartphone-based facial scanning
  • Frames made around individual measurements
  • Multiple styles and color options
  • Prescription-ready designs
Check Availability

8. Ray-Ban Remix

Ray-Ban Remix takes customization into the build-your-own category. Rather than creating a modular frame that can be modified after purchase, Remix allows shoppers to personalize selected Ray-Ban styles before ordering. Depending on the model and current availability, customers can choose from different frame colors, lens options, and other design details.

The appeal is the ability to create a personalized version of a familiar silhouette rather than settling for one of the standard combinations typically available in stores. It’s a different experience from Pair or Funoogles, but it still qualifies as meaningful customization because the customer is actively designing the final product rather than simply selecting an off-the-shelf pair.

Highlights

  • Custom frame and lens combinations
  • Personalization available on eligible models
  • Built around iconic Ray-Ban silhouettes
  • Virtual try-on available for supported products
Check Availability

Buying Guide: How to Choose a Customizable Eyewear Brand

Decide what you actually want to customize. If you want to change the appearance of your glasses regularly, look at interchangeable systems such as Pair Eyewear, Funoogles, or ro•sham•bo Pops. If you want different optical performance from the same sunglasses, Switch Vision’s interchangeable lenses are a better fit. Fitz Frames focuses on personalized fit, while Ray-Ban Remix lets you create a customized configuration before ordering.

Choose Casual Sneakers
Source Industrial Parts

Check prescription compatibility early. Not every customizable system supports every prescription or lens configuration. This is especially important with interchangeable lenses and specialized frame designs. If you have a strong prescription, confirm compatibility with the exact frame and lens combination before purchasing.

Consider the total cost, not just the starting price. With modular eyewear, the base frame is only part of the equation. Additional Tops, clips, or lenses can add to the total, so compare what a realistic collection will cost rather than judging a system solely by its entry price.

Think about how much flexibility you actually need. If you want multiple fashion looks from one pair, an interchangeable system offers the most flexibility. If your priority is comfort, custom-fit eyewear may be more valuable. And if you’re primarily interested in adapting sunglasses to changing conditions, interchangeable lenses solve a different problem altogether.

Don’t overlook lens quality. Customization is only one part of a good pair of glasses. Prescription accuracy, lens material, coatings, UV protection, polarization, and optical performance should all factor into the decision, especially if the glasses will be worn every day.

Understand the difference between customization and configuration. A product can be customized before purchase without being designed for modification afterward. Pair and Funoogles offer the clearest examples of interchangeable customization, while Fitz Frames focuses on custom fit and Ray-Ban Remix on build-to-order personalization.

Final Thoughts

Customizable eyewear has evolved beyond simply offering glasses in a few different colors. Today’s options range from magnetic interchangeable frames and clips to swappable lenses, personalized facial measurements, and build-your-own configurations.

Pair Eyewear is the strongest all-around choice for people who want to change their look regularly, while Funoogles brings that same interchangeable concept to children’s eyewear. ro•sham•bo’s Pops line combines interchangeable components with a durability-focused design, and Switch Vision applies the concept to functional lens changes for outdoor activities.

Fitz Frames takes a different approach by customizing the fit around the wearer, while Ray-Ban Remix lets shoppers personalize selected classic silhouettes before ordering. The best choice ultimately depends on what you want customization to accomplish — whether that’s more fashion variety, greater functionality, a better fit, or simply a more personal version of a familiar frame.

The important thing is that “customizable” no longer has to mean just picking a color. For shoppers who want eyewear that feels more personal and adaptable, these eight brands offer some of the clearest ways to make glasses your own in 2026.
